baseline: First brush/UI pass, recorded in brush-ux-audit-20261022.json; second-pass display comparator is its frozen executable. Timelapse reference is the original full-frame algorithm in the same final test binary.

timelapse.scope: Three sequential full/banded trials per case in the same build; opaque RGB output verified byte-for-byte outside timing. Band bytes exclude output RGB, compositing scratch, source snapshots and allocator overhead; not RSS or pen latency.

sparse_4096_display.scope: CPU texture payload and theoretical mip bytes; excludes GPU/driver allocation overhead and source/compositor memory. One sequential run, not physical input latency.

display_comparison.method: One sequential frozen baseline and final run, 48 cases each, without concurrent compiler jobs. Descriptive CPU timings; no statistical speedup claim. Exact padded pixels, snapshot preservation, coherent publication, and upload accounting verified by the benchmark.
display_comparison.scope: Supported 512/2048-square documents: one dense flat base plus sparse additional layers, 1/8/32 layers; eager padded display shared with navigator. Synchronous comparator and production background tile compositor using existing parallel pixel bands; sliced cursor is failure fallback. Owner 2 ms allowance checked between controls/publications, which can overrun. One sequential drain per case; 1 ms polling sleeps when awaiting worker, no UI frame waits. Owner update timings exclude worker execution; completed-worker milliseconds sum kernel elapsed wall time, not all-core CPU time. Drain wall includes polling and image reconstruction, excludes final pixel oracle. Every padded pixel and emitted-payload accounting checked outside call timing. Texture bytes are RGBA payload with theoretical complete mip chain, not measured GPU allocation. Metadata/prefix bytes count owned vector capacities, excluding weak allocation headers/allocator overhead. Preparation peak estimates worker output capacity plus imaging buffers and per-frame pending canvas image payload, excludes frozen source snapshots, resident cache/history/document and validation copies. This is not RSS, a total memory budget or dense 32-layer certification.
display_comparison.publication_scope: Sliced preparation holds one frozen document for the entire tile generation; continuous newer edits request a successor instead of restarting it. Canvas and navigator draw the same complete published handles. Static benchmark phases verify that drawable presentation stays on the previous complete set until all new handles publish together, then compare every presented padded pixel with the compositor. Initial and resized frames remain blank until complete; resize must free all incompatible old texture IDs on the first update. Both prepared and presented texture IDs count once when shared; sampled peaks include retained old handles during same-size replacement, but can miss a transient within one owner call. RGBA and complete mip-chain capacities are theoretical, not GPU/RSS measurements or a residency budget. Frozen generation and active/retired worker sources participate in snapshot deduplication; a canceled retiring worker prevents a new generation source from being captured until it exits. GUI/input latency and continuous-edit performance are covered only by separate functional tests, not these timings.
display_comparison.snapshot_scope: Non-owning allocation IDs/capacities describe pending immutable sources; handles already finished are excluded. Per-call source sampling is outside owner timing and may miss a short-lived source. Pixel bytes are deduplicated beyond the live document, and may also be shared with history/save. Metadata describes cloned document/name/layer capacities. Descriptor vectors are separate display metadata. Counts are conservative while a worker exits, not RSS or a global memory budget. Snapshot probes hold two real snapshots across one pixel edit, verify unchanged source RGBA and sharing, and compare tiled versus flat compatibility; extra layers are sparse.

limits: Texture bytes are RGBA payload and theoretical mip payload, not physical VRAM or process RAM; driver allocation and per-handle overhead excluded.
Timelapse band bytes exclude RGB output, source snapshots, compositor scratch and allocator overhead.
First nonuniform edits expand compact tiles with a full padded upload. Fully nonuniform canvases retain the original display budget; general viewport residency is not implemented.
512-square timelapse fixture is blank; its dab is outside the document. Larger sparse fixtures contain one dab.
No physical tablet latency or sustained native GPU acceptance claim.
